CVE-2026-62151.title: mysql_fdw SQL injection through a multi-byte character set escaping bypass
CVE-2026-62151.description: mysql_fdw builds string literals for queries sent to the remote MySQL server with an escaping routine that is not character-set aware. When the connection uses a multi-byte character set such as GBK, SJIS or Big5 and MySQL's default backslash escaping is in effect, a crafted value whose trailing byte is 0x5C absorbs the escaping backslash and leaves the following quote unescaped. The routine handles every pushed-down string constant, including ordinary WHERE-clause literals, so an authenticated user with only SELECT on a foreign table can break out of the literal and run arbitrary SQL on the remote MySQL server with the credentials of the user mapping. The issue is fixed in mysql_fdw 2.10.0. From mysql_fdw 2.10.0, mysql_fdw forces NO_BACKSLASH_ESCAPES into the session sql_mode and escapes string literals by doubling single quotes.

net: restore refcount ordering for lockless socket access

CVE-2026-99742.title: mm/mempolicy: charge shared policy nodes
CVE-2026-99742.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

mm/mempolicy: charge shared policy nodes

Any local user can bypass memory.max with mbind() on a tmpfs file, and
allocate unbounded kernel memory.

mbind() sets a NUMA memory policy for a range of a mapping. If the
mapping is of a shmem and friends, the kernel also stores the policy on
the inode, in a tree with one entry per range of the file.

Each mbind() on a single page of a mapping can add one shared policy node
(struct sp_node) and one struct mempolicy to that tree. They outlive the
mapping and stay around until the inode is destroyed. The tree is not
bounded by the file size, so the file can be empty.

Memory that user space can allocate must be charged to a memory cgroup. A
slab cache does that for all of its objects if it is created with
SLAB_ACCOUNT. numa_policy_init() creates the slab caches for both
structs without SLAB_ACCOUNT, so they are not charged to any cgroup.
